text: Working on the proxy.go bug (balancer with no targets panics instead of returning 503). A subagent is diagnosing and fixing it now; I'll confirm once the fix is verified against the full test suite.

It goes to the Echo instance's logger output, not to stdout directly.

In `LoggerWithConfig` (middleware/logger.go), the config is defaulted at construction: `if config.Output == nil { config.Output = DefaultLoggerConfig.Output }` (lines 95-97), and `DefaultLoggerConfig` never sets `Output`, so it stays nil. At write time the nil check is repeated (lines 215-218):

```go
if config.Output == nil {
    _, err = c.Logger().Output().Write(buf.Bytes())
    return
}
_, err = config.Output.Write(buf.Bytes())
```

So with a nil `Output` the line is written to `c.Logger().Output()` — the `echo.Logger` of the Echo instance handling the request (i.e. `e.Logger.Output()`, which is `os.Stdout` unless the app called `e.Logger.SetOutput(...)`). Note the colorer is also built with that nil writer (`config.colorer.SetOutput(config.Output)` at line 101), so color codes are disabled/ignored in that case.

Fix is in: middleware/proxy.go now returns nil from both balancers' Next() when the target list is empty, and the Proxy middleware returns echo.ErrServiceUnavailable (503) instead of panicking. Full test suite passes. An independent verification run is in progress; I'll confirm shortly.
Started on the router.go bug (non-routable paths). A subagent is reproducing and fixing it now; I'll report the fix and verification.

Bug #1 fixed and independently verified.

Cause: both balancers in middleware/proxy.go indexed into `targets` without a length check, so a balancer with zero targets panicked (`Intn(0)` / integer divide by zero) and the middleware then dereferenced a nil target.

Fix (middleware/proxy.go only, 11 lines added, no API change):
- `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now return nil when `len(b.targets) == 0` (round-robin also takes the read lock while reading `targets`).
- `ProxyWithConfig` returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) when the selected target is nil, instead of panicking.

Verified: full suite `go test ./...` (and `-race`) green, gofmt/vet/build clean, no pre-existing test modified, no new files in the repo. An out-of-repo test confirmed 503 for empty slice, nil slice, targets emptied via RemoveTarget, and a custom balancer returning nil; the same test against the original code panicked, confirming causality. A pre-existing (unrelated, not regressed) data race on `roundRobinBalancer.i` under concurrent Next() remains — outside this bug's scope.

`MethodOverride()` returns `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)` — i.e. an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` (the middleware configured with the defaults: `Skipper: DefaultSkipper` and `Getter: MethodFromHeader(echo.HeaderXHTTPMethodOverride)`, so it reads the override from the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header).

The returned middleware only overrides the method when the incoming request method is `POST` and the getter returns a non-empty string; otherwise it just calls `next(c)` (middleware/method_override.go lines 37-39 and 52-66).
#1 is fixed and verified (see my earlier confirmation): middleware/proxy.go no longer panics with a zero-target balancer and returns 503.

It is `DefaultSkipper` (middleware/body_dump.go, lines 34-39):

```go
DefaultBodyDumpConfig = BodyDumpConfig{
	Skipper: DefaultSkipper,
}
```

`DefaultSkipper` is the package-level skipper defined in middleware/middleware.go that always returns `false`, so the BodyDump middleware is never skipped by default. (`BodyDumpWithConfig` also re-defaults to `DefaultBodyDumpConfig.Skipper` when `config.Skipper` is nil, and panics if `config.Handler` is nil.)

It sets it to `DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper` (middleware/decompress.go, lines 76-78):

```go
if config.Skipper == nil {
	config.Skipper = DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper
}
```

So it borrows the Skipper from the *Gzip* (compress) config rather than `DefaultDecompressConfig.Skipper`. Both are in fact `DefaultSkipper`, so the effective behavior is the same, but the reference is the wrong config (a copy/paste slip, same pattern as in redirect.go).

It panics (middleware/body_limit.go, lines 61-65):

```go
limit, err := bytes.Parse(config.Limit)
if err != nil {
	panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit))
}
config.limit = limit
```

So an unparsable `Limit` (e.g. `"4x"`-style value that `gommon/bytes.Parse` rejects) causes `BodyLimitWithConfig` to panic with `fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit)` at middleware-construction time, rather than returning an error. Note `BodyLimit(limit)` passes the limit through to this same function, so it panics too.
